title: Many Cultures, One City
text:
Our city has people from many countries. In my class, students speak Turkish, Arabic, English and Spanish. We often share food from our homes. Every festival is a chance to learn about a new culture.

Some people think that differences make life hard. But my friends say differences make life more interesting. When we listen to each other, we learn new words and ideas. Diversity makes our community stronger.

questions.text: Which languages do the students in the writer's class speak?
According to paragraph two, what do the writer's friends say about differences?
options: They are not important at all

questions.text: What does the writer think about cultural diversity?
options: It is a positive thing for a community
It is a problem that should be avoided
It is important only during festivals
It is something only children enjoy

questions.text: Why do the students share food from their homes?
options: To learn about each other's cultures
Because the school forces them to
Because they do not like school food

vocabulary.definition: a special event or celebration, often with music and food
the customs, beliefs and way of life of a group of people
a range of different people, ideas or things
a group of people who live or work together

paragraph_translations: Şehrimizde birçok ülkeden insanlar yaşıyor. Benim sınıfımda öğrenciler Türkçe, Arapça, İngilizce ve İspanyolca konuşuyor. Genellikle evlerimizden yemek paylaşırız. Her festival, yeni bir kültürü öğrenmek için bir fırsattır.

Bazı insanlar farklılıkların hayatı zorlaştırdığını düşünüyor. Ama arkadaşlarım farklılıkların hayatı daha ilginç hale getirdiğini söylüyor. Birbirimizi dinlediğimizde yeni kelimeler ve fikirler öğreniriz. Çeşitlilik topluluğumuzu daha güçlü yapar.
